Which companies worry about tariffs on i.answer: Many S&P 100 companies discuss tariffs, and 61 of 102 added or expanded tariff and trade language this year, though that count covers tariffs generally, not only China. The filings that tie tariffs to China specifically include Eli Lilly, which cites "new tariffs on Chinese goods" and China's retaliatory tariffs [1], and PepsiCo, which lists tariffs on China among those affecting its input costs [2]. Ford points to China's restrictions on rare earth exports alongside tariffs [3], and Deere says most of its rare earth minerals come from China [4]. Tesla [5] and Intuitive Surgical [6] also flag trade changes with China and tariffs as risks.

How does JPMorgan describe the risk of a.answer: JPMorgan treats cyberattacks as a major, growing risk. Its main cyber risk factor, "A successful cyber attack could cause significant harm to JPMorganChase and its clients and customers," was rewritten this year. It warns that the bank "could become increasingly vulnerable to cyber attacks" if it does not promptly fix emerging threats or control weaknesses, and it names specific threats such as zero-day vulnerabilities, distributed denial-of-service attacks, malware and ransomware, and insider misuse [1][2][3][4]. A separate risk says that its growing links with clients, vendors and other outside parties "increases the risk of failure or cyber attacks" on those systems [5][6]. The bank also says it "has experienced and expects that it will continue to experience failures and disruptions" in its systems, and that some of these incidents have led to customer personal data being taken [7][8].
